text: A new hemoglobin with increased oxygen affinity, beta82 (EF6) lysine, leads to threonine (Hb Rahere), was discovered during the investigation of a patient whose haemoglobin concentration was elevated after a routine blood count. The substitution affects one of the two, three-phosphate-glycerate binding sites, leading to an increased affinity for oxygen, but both the hemoglobin-hemoglobin interaction and the alkaline Bohr effect remain normal in the haemolysate. This variant has the same mobility as hemoglobin A on electrophoresis at alkaline pH but can be detected by measuring the whole-blood oxygen affinity; however, it cannot be separated from hemoglobin A using electrophoresis in agar at acidic pH. The elevated haemoglobin concentration was primarily attributed to a decrease in plasma volume (relative polycythemia) and was accompanied by a persistently high white blood cell count. This case underscores the importance of measuring the oxygen affinity of hemoglobin in all patients with absolute or relative polycythemia when no apparent cause is identified.
